result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_vertex_cover()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if a set of nodes touches every edge (a vertex cover). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L58489-L58536){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_vertex_cover(nodes) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Is vertex cover](/assets/graphs/is-vertex-cover.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A star with center hub and leaves a, b, c on both sides, with the candidate nodes outlined. Left: hub touches every edge, so is_vertex_cover() returns True. Right: the leaf a alone leaves the edges hub-b and hub-c (shown in the accent color) untouched, so is_vertex_cover() returns False." width="100%"} A vertex cover is a set of nodes such that every edge has at least one endpoint in the set. It is the complement of an independent set: a set of nodes is a vertex cover exactly when the remaining nodes have no edges among them. Use this method to validate the output of `bipartite_vertex_cover()` or `min_weighted_vertex_cover()`, or a hand-picked set of monitors. Edge direction is ignored, and a self-loop is only covered by its own node. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of node IDs or labels. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if every edge has an endpoint in `nodes`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node does not exist. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} One pass over the edge list in $O(V + E)$ time. ## Examples {.doc-examples} The center of a star covers every edge; any leaves alone do not: ::: {#8f8d5ba0 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["hub", "a", "b", "c"]) g.add_edges([("hub", "a"), ("hub", "b"), ("hub", "c")]) g.is_vertex_cover(["hub"]), g.is_vertex_cover(["a", "b", "c"]), g.is_vertex_cover(["a"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (True, True, False) ``` ::: :::
